limitations_and_boundaries: The study uses a specific cell line (RPE1-hTERT) and inducible TRF2-DN to model telomere crisis; generalizability to other cell types or in vivo contexts is not addressed.
Chromothripsis and kataegis were observed in a subset of post-crisis clones; the factors determining which clones develop these features are not fully elucidated.
TREX1-independent mechanisms of bridge resolution exist but are not characterized.
The study does not directly demonstrate that chromothripsis and kataegis occur in the same cell that experienced a chromatin bridge, only that they are present in post-crisis populations.
The role of APOBEC enzymes in generating kataegis is inferred from mutation signatures but not directly tested.
The selected source chunks do not report a rescue, reconstitution, reversal, or epistasis experiment; that rung of the causal evidence chain remains untested within this extraction scope.
